fields.title: From Roles to Attributes
fields.keyTakeaway: Roles plus scope plus a few named restrictions cover almost all requests, while delegation and temporary access are needed by almost everyone and usually forgotten.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: A client asks: "a manager sees their stores, but only orders over 5 thousand, and only during working hours." How do you express this?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: The access model determines who the product can serve. Too simple loses clients, too flexible loses clarity. Moving between levels takes months, so the level must be chosen deliberately.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: **[[rbac|Role-based model]]** — permissions through roles, roles assigned to people. Clear, configurable, covers the majority. Covered in `SE1-N1-L2`.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: **[[abac|Attribute-based model]]** — permissions computed from attributes: who the subject is, what the object is, under what conditions. Lets you express the example from the question. The cost — rules become code written by non-programmers, and understanding why access exists or not is difficult.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: The practical middle ground most products arrive at: **roles plus scope plus a small set of named restrictions.** Not arbitrary rules, but pre-thought-out toggles: "only own stores", "no buyer personal data", "read-only".
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: Three mechanisms that almost everyone needs and often forgets:
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: **[[delegation|Delegation]].** A manager leaves and hands over rights to a deputy. Without a mechanism this is done by sharing a password — meaning turning off the entire access model at once.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: **[[just-in-time-access|Temporary access]].** Rights for a duration tied to a task. Especially for our own support: an employee gets access to a client account for two hours with a justification, rather than permanently.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: **[[guest-access|Guest access]].** An external participant — auditor, contractor — with a limited set.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: And the **[[separation-of-duties|separation of duties]]** principle: one person should not perform an entire sensitive process. The one who adds a supplier should not approve payouts to them.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: The "roles plus scope" model from `SE1` is supplemented by three toggle constraints:
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: *No buyer personal data* — for accountants and analysts. *Read-only* — for auditors and interns. *Only own stores* — for managers in chains with complex structures.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: The attribute model was not built: out of 900 partners, arbitrary rules were requested by two, and both had enough with the combination of toggles.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: Delegation was added after discovering that 11% of active sessions in partner accounts came from devices other than normal for that account — a sign of password sharing. The "transfer rights for a period" mechanism closed this.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: Temporary access for our support: an employee requests access to a partner account, provides the ticket number, gets it for two hours. Everything is logged. Before this, support had permanent access to all accounts — classic [[excessive-privileges|excessive privileges]].
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Model flexibility is limited by the client's ability to configure it. A model requiring training will not be used correctly.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Roles plus scope plus a few named restrictions cover almost all requests, while delegation and temporary access are needed by almost everyone and usually forgotten.
